avoid_supplements.name: Iron supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Sucroferric oxyhydroxide contains iron and binds phosphate; concurrent iron supplementation increases iron burden and hyperferremia risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid all iron supplements unless specifically prescribed by physician for documented deficiency; obtain serum iron levels

avoid_supplements.name: Calcium supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Both agents bind phosphate and may compete for absorption; additive effects increase hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia control unpredictability
avoid_supplements.action: Space dosing by at least 2 hours; consult nephrologist before concurrent use

avoid_supplements.name: Zinc supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Sucroferric oxyhydroxide may impair zinc absorption through binding and pH alterations in the GI tract
avoid_supplements.action: Monitor zinc levels; supplement only if deficiency confirmed; separate dosing by 2+ hours

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential for additive effects on phosphate binding and possible magnesium malabsorption
caution_supplements.action: Monitor serum magnesium levels periodically; adjust dose if hypomagnesemia develops

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin D supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: May interact with phosphate-calcium-vitamin D metabolism in chronic kidney disease patients
caution_supplements.action: Coordinate dosing with nephrologist; monitor calcium-phosphate product

avoid_foods.name: High-phosphate foods (processed meats, dairy, cola beverages)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Sucroferric oxyhydroxide is indicated to reduce phosphate absorption; high dietary phosphate overwhelming drug efficacy reduces therapeutic benefit
avoid_foods.action: Educate patient on phosphate-restricted diet; refer to renal nutritionist for CKD-appropriate meal planning

caution_foods.name: Iron-rich foods (red meat, fortified cereals, spinach)
caution_foods.mechanism: Drug contains iron; high dietary iron may contribute to cumulative iron load, particularly in dialysis patients
caution_foods.action: Monitor serum ferritin and transferrin saturation; moderate red meat consumption if elevated iron stores

caution_foods.name: Calcium-fortified foods
caution_foods.mechanism: Additive effects with phosphate binding; may affect mineral metabolism balance
caution_foods.action: Track total dietary and supplemental calcium intake; coordinate with nephrologist

monitoring_notes: Monitor serum phosphate, calcium, iron panel (ferritin, transferrin saturation), and zinc levels regularly, especially in the first 1-3 months of therapy. Patient education on strict phosphate restriction and adherence is critical for efficacy in chronic kidney disease management.
